passages.text: “If a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters or sells it, he must repay five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.
passages.sermon:
A man may steal an ox or a sheep.
He may slaughter the animal.
He may sell the animal.
If he does this, he must repay for what he took.
He must give five oxen for each ox he stole.
He must give four sheep for each sheep he stole.
passages.original: כִּ֤י יִגְנֹֽב־ אִישׁ֙ שׁ֣וֹר אוֹ־ שֶׂ֔ה וּטְבָח֖וֹ א֣וֹ מְכָר֑וֹ חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה בָקָ֗ר יְשַׁלֵּם֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשּׁ֔וֹר וְאַרְבַּע־ צֹ֖אן תַּ֥חַת הַשֶּֽׂה׃

passages.text: If a thief is caught breaking in and is beaten to death, no one shall be guilty of bloodshed.
passages.sermon:
A thief breaks into a house.
Someone catches the thief during the break-in.
Someone strikes the thief.
The thief dies from the blow.
No one is guilty of murder in this case.
passages.original: אִם־ בַּמַּחְתֶּ֛רֶת יִמָּצֵ֥א הַגַּנָּ֖ב וְהֻכָּ֣ה וָמֵ֑ת אֵ֥ין ל֖וֹ דָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: But if it happens after sunrise, there is guilt for his bloodshed. A thief must make full restitution; if he has nothing, he himself shall be sold for his theft.
passages.sermon:
This law speaks about a thief.
If someone catches a thief after sunrise, and kills him, the person is guilty of bloodshed.
The thief must pay back everything he stole.
If the thief cannot pay back, he must be sold to pay for his theft.
passages.original: אִם־ זָרְחָ֥ה הַשֶּׁ֛מֶשׁ עָלָ֖יו דָּמִ֣ים ל֑וֹ שַׁלֵּ֣ם יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם אִם־ אֵ֣ין ל֔וֹ וְנִמְכַּ֖ר בִּגְנֵבָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If what was stolen is actually found alive in his possession—whether ox or donkey or sheep—he must pay back double.
passages.sermon:
A thief steals an animal.
Someone finds the stolen animal alive with the thief.
The animal can be an ox, a donkey, or a sheep.
The thief must pay back double the value of the animal.
passages.original: אִֽם־ הִמָּצֵא֩ תִמָּצֵ֨א בְיָד֜וֹ הַגְּנֵבָ֗ה מִשּׁ֧וֹר עַד־ חֲמ֛וֹר עַד־ שֶׂ֖ה חַיִּ֑ים שְׁנַ֖יִם יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃ס

passages.text: If a man grazes his livestock in a field or vineyard and allows them to stray so that they graze in someone else’s field, he must make restitution from the best of his own field or vineyard.
passages.sermon:
A man owns livestock.
He lets his animals graze in his own field or vineyard.
He allows his animals to wander into another person's field.
His animals eat crops in that other person's field.
The man must pay for the damage.
He must give the best produce from his own field or vineyard as payment.
passages.original: כִּ֤י יַבְעֶר־ אִישׁ֙ שָׂדֶ֣ה אוֹ־ כֶ֔רֶם וְשִׁלַּח֙ אֶת־ בְּעִירֹה וּבִעֵ֖ר בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה אַחֵ֑ר מֵיטַ֥ב שָׂדֵ֛הוּ וּמֵיטַ֥ב כַּרְמ֖וֹ יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃ס

passages.text: If a fire breaks out and spreads to thornbushes so that it consumes stacked or standing grain, or the whole field, the one who started the fire must make full restitution.
passages.sermon:
This law speaks about responsibility for causing damage by fire.
If a person starts a fire, he is responsible for what happens next.
If the fire spreads to thornbushes, it can cause more damage.
If the fire burns stacked grain, the person who started the fire is responsible.
If the fire burns standing grain, the person who started the fire is responsible.
If the fire burns the whole field, the person who started the fire is responsible.
The person who started the fire must pay for all the damage.
He must make full restitution for what was destroyed.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תֵצֵ֨א אֵ֜שׁ וּמָצְאָ֤ה קֹצִים֙ וְנֶאֱכַ֣ל גָּדִ֔ישׁ א֥וֹ הַקָּמָ֖ה א֣וֹ הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה שַׁלֵּ֣ם יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם הַמַּבְעִ֖ר אֶת־ הַבְּעֵרָֽה׃ס

passages.text: If a man gives his neighbor money or goods for safekeeping and they are stolen from the neighbor’s house, the thief, if caught, must pay back double.
passages.sermon: A man gives his neighbor money or goods to keep safe.\r\nSomeone steals the money or goods from the neighbor’s house.\r\nIf the thief is caught, the thief must pay back double.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יִתֵּן֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶל־ רֵעֵ֜הוּ כֶּ֤סֶף אֽוֹ־ כֵלִים֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔ר וְגֻנַּ֖ב מִבֵּ֣ית הָאִ֑ישׁ אִם־ יִמָּצֵ֥א הַגַּנָּ֖ב יְשַׁלֵּ֥ם שְׁנָֽיִם׃

passages.text: If the thief is not found, the owner of the house must appear before the judges to determine whether he has taken his neighbor’s property.
passages.sermon: If someone’s property is stolen from his neighbor’s house, and the thief is not found, the owner of the house must go before the judges.\r\nThe judges will decide if the owner took his neighbor’s property or not.
passages.original: אִם־ לֹ֤א יִמָּצֵא֙ הַגַּנָּ֔ב וְנִקְרַ֥ב בַּֽעַל־ הַבַּ֖יִת אֶל־ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים אִם־ לֹ֥א שָׁלַ֛ח יָד֖וֹ בִּמְלֶ֥אכֶת רֵעֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: In all cases of illegal possession of an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost item that someone claims, ‘This is mine,’ both parties shall bring their cases before the judges. The one whom the judges find guilty must pay back double to his neighbor.
passages.sermon:
This law speaks about disputes over property.
It includes cases of illegal possession.
It covers an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost item.
Someone may claim, “This is mine.”
Both people must go before the judges.
The judges will hear both sides.
The judges will decide who is guilty.
The guilty person must pay back double to his neighbor.
passages.original: עַֽל־ כָּל־ דְּבַר־ פֶּ֡שַׁע עַל־ שׁ֡וֹר עַל־ חֲ֠מוֹר עַל־ שֶׂ֨ה עַל־ שַׂלְמָ֜ה עַל־ כָּל־ אֲבֵדָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֹאמַר֙ כִּי־ ה֣וּא זֶ֔ה עַ֚ד הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים יָבֹ֖א דְּבַר־ שְׁנֵיהֶ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַרְשִׁיעֻן֙ אֱלֹהִ֔ים יְשַׁלֵּ֥ם שְׁנַ֖יִם לְרֵעֵֽהוּ׃ס

passages.text: If a man gives a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any other animal to be cared for by his neighbor, but it dies or is injured or stolen while no one is watching, an oath before the LORD shall be made between the parties to determine whether or not the man has taken his neighbor’s property. The owner must accept the oath and require no restitution.
passages.sermon:
A man may give his neighbor an animal to care for.
The animal may be a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any other kind of animal.
The neighbor must watch over the animal.
Sometimes the animal may die.
Sometimes the animal may be injured.
Sometimes the animal may be stolen.
No one may see what happened to the animal.
In this case, both men must come before the LORD.
They must make an oath before the LORD.
The oath will show if the neighbor took his friend’s property or not.
If the neighbor did not take the animal, the oath will prove it.
The owner must accept the oath.
The neighbor does not have to pay anything back.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יִתֵּן֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶל־ רֵעֵ֜הוּ חֲמ֨וֹר אוֹ־ שׁ֥וֹר אוֹ־ שֶׂ֛ה וְכָל־ בְּהֵמָ֖ה לִשְׁמֹ֑ר וּמֵ֛ת אוֹ־ נִשְׁבַּ֥ר אוֹ־ נִשְׁבָּ֖ה אֵ֥ין רֹאֶֽה׃ שְׁבֻעַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה תִּהְיֶה֙ בֵּ֣ין שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם אִם־ לֹ֥א שָׁלַ֛ח יָד֖וֹ בִּמְלֶ֣אכֶת רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְלָקַ֥ח בְּעָלָ֖יו וְלֹ֥א יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃

passages.text: But if the animal was actually stolen from the neighbor, he must make restitution to the owner.
passages.sermon: If someone is caring for his neighbor’s animal, and the animal is stolen from him,\r\nhe must pay the owner for the loss.\r\nHe must make restitution to the owner.
passages.original: וְאִם־ גָּנֹ֥ב יִגָּנֵ֖ב מֵעִמּ֑וֹ יְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לִבְעָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: If the animal was torn to pieces, he shall bring it as evidence; he need not make restitution for the torn carcass.
passages.sermon:
A man cares for his neighbor’s animal.
The animal is torn to pieces by a wild beast.
The man brings the torn carcass as evidence.
He does not need to pay for the animal.
passages.original: אִם־ טָרֹ֥ף יִטָּרֵ֖ף יְבִאֵ֣הוּ עֵ֑ד הַטְּרֵפָ֖ה לֹ֥א יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃פ

passages.text: If a man borrows an animal from his neighbor and it is injured or dies while its owner is not present, he must make full restitution.
passages.sermon:
A man borrows an animal from his neighbor.
The animal is injured or dies.
The owner is not present.
The borrower must pay the owner in full for the loss.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יִשְׁאַ֥ל אִ֛ישׁ מֵעִ֥ם רֵעֵ֖הוּ וְנִשְׁבַּ֣ר אוֹ־ מֵ֑ת בְּעָלָ֥יו אֵין־ עִמּ֖וֹ שַׁלֵּ֥ם יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃

passages.text: If the owner was present, no restitution is required. If the animal was rented, the fee covers the loss.
passages.sermon: If the owner was present, the borrower does not pay for the loss.\r\nIf the animal was rented, the rental fee covers the loss.
passages.original: אִם־ בְּעָלָ֥יו עִמּ֖וֹ לֹ֣א יְשַׁלֵּ֑ם אִם־ שָׂכִ֣יר ה֔וּא בָּ֖א בִּשְׂכָרֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: If a man seduces a virgin who is not pledged in marriage and sleeps with her, he must pay the full dowry for her to be his wife.
passages.sermon:
A man may seduce a virgin.
This virgin is not pledged to be married.
The man sleeps with her.
He must pay the full dowry for her.
He must take her to be his wife.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יְפַתֶּ֣ה אִ֗ישׁ בְּתוּלָ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ אֹרָ֖שָׂה וְשָׁכַ֣ב עִמָּ֑הּ מָהֹ֛ר יִמְהָרֶ֥נָּה לּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, the man still must pay an amount comparable to the bridal price of a virgin.
passages.sermon:
A man seduces a virgin who is not pledged in marriage.
He sleeps with her.
He must pay the full dowry for her to be his wife.
If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him,
the man must still pay an amount equal to the bridal price of a virgin.
passages.original: אִם־ מָאֵ֧ן יְמָאֵ֛ן אָבִ֖יהָ לְתִתָּ֣הּ ל֑וֹ כֶּ֣סֶף יִשְׁקֹ֔ל כְּמֹ֖הַר הַבְּתוּלֹֽת׃ס

passages.text: You must not allow a sorceress to live.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to Israel.
A sorceress is a woman who practices sorcery.
Sorcery means using magic or occult powers.
God said, “Do not let a sorceress live.”
The people must not allow a sorceress to remain alive.
passages.original: מְכַשֵּׁפָ֖ה לֹ֥א תְחַיֶּֽה׃ס

passages.text: Whoever lies with an animal must surely be put to death.
passages.sermon:
This law comes from God.
\r\nGod gave this law to Israel.
\r\nGod says, “Whoever lies with an animal must be put to death.”
\r\nIf a person has sexual relations with an animal, that person must die.
\r\nGod commands this punishment.
passages.original: כָּל־ שֹׁכֵ֥ב עִם־ בְּהֵמָ֖ה מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃ס

passages.text: If anyone sacrifices to any god other than the LORD alone, he must be set apart for destruction.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to Israel.
God is the LORD.
The LORD is the only true God.
If a person sacrifices to any god except the LORD,
That person must be set apart for destruction.
passages.original: זֹבֵ֥חַ לָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יָֽחֳרָ֑ם בִּלְתִּ֥י לַיהוָ֖ה לְבַדּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: You must not exploit or oppress a foreign resident, for you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to Israel.
God said, “Do not exploit a foreign resident.
Do not oppress a foreign resident.
You were foreigners in Egypt.
You know what it feels like to be a foreigner.
Treat foreign residents with kindness and fairness.”
passages.original: וְגֵ֥ר לֹא־ תוֹנֶ֖ה וְלֹ֣א תִלְחָצֶ֑נּוּ כִּֽי־ גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: You must not mistreat any widow or orphan.
passages.sermon: God gave this command to His people.\r\nGod said, “Do not mistreat any widow.”\r\nGod said, “Do not mistreat any orphan.”
passages.original: כָּל־ אַלְמָנָ֥ה וְיָת֖וֹם לֹ֥א תְעַנּֽוּן׃

passages.text: If you do mistreat them, and they cry out to Me in distress, I will surely hear their cry.
passages.sermon: God commands His people not to mistreat widows, orphans, or foreigners.\r\nIf you mistreat them, they may cry out to God.\r\nIf they cry out to God, He will hear their cry.
passages.original: אִם־ עַנֵּ֥ה תְעַנֶּ֖ה אֹת֑וֹ כִּ֣י אִם־ צָעֹ֤ק יִצְעַק֙ אֵלַ֔י שָׁמֹ֥עַ אֶשְׁמַ֖ע צַעֲקָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: My anger will be kindled, and I will kill you with the sword; then your wives will become widows and your children will be fatherless.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God warns about mistreating widows and orphans.
God says, “My anger will burn against you.”
God says, “I will kill you with the sword.”
God says, “Your wives will become widows.”
God says, “Your children will become orphans.”
passages.original: וְחָרָ֣ה אַפִּ֔י וְהָרַגְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם בֶּחָ֑רֶב וְהָי֤וּ נְשֵׁיכֶם֙ אַלְמָנ֔וֹת וּבְנֵיכֶ֖ם יְתֹמִֽים׃פ

passages.text: If you lend money to one of My people among you who is poor, you must not act as a creditor to him; you are not to charge him interest.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God cares for the poor among His people.
If you lend money to a poor person among My people,
do not act as a harsh creditor to him.
Do not charge him interest.
passages.original: אִם־ כֶּ֣סֶף׀ תַּלְוֶ֣ה אֶת־ עַמִּ֗י אֶת־ הֶֽעָנִי֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ לֹא־ תִהְיֶ֥ה ל֖וֹ כְּנֹשֶׁ֑ה לֹֽא־ תְשִׂימ֥וּן עָלָ֖יו נֶֽשֶׁךְ׃

passages.text: If you take your neighbor’s cloak as collateral, return it to him by sunset, because his cloak is the only covering he has for his body. What else will he sleep in? And if he cries out to Me, I will hear, for I am compassionate.
passages.sermon:
God is compassionate.
God cares for the poor and vulnerable.
If you take your neighbor’s cloak as collateral, you must return it to him by sunset.
His cloak is his only covering.
His cloak is the only garment for his body.
He has nothing else to sleep in.
If your neighbor cries out to God, God will hear him.
God listens because He is compassionate.
passages.original: אִם־ חָבֹ֥ל תַּחְבֹּ֖ל שַׂלְמַ֣ת רֵעֶ֑ךָ עַד־ בֹּ֥א הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ תְּשִׁיבֶ֥נּוּ לֽוֹ׃ כִּ֣י הִ֤וא כְסוּתָה לְבַדָּ֔הּ הִ֥וא שִׂמְלָת֖וֹ לְעֹר֑וֹ בַּמֶּ֣ה יִשְׁכָּ֔ב וְהָיָה֙ כִּֽי־ יִצְעַ֣ק אֵלַ֔י וְשָׁמַעְתִּ֖י כִּֽי־ חַנּ֥וּן אָֽנִי׃ס

passages.text: You must not blaspheme God or curse the ruler of your people.
passages.sermon: God commands His people.\r\nDo not blaspheme God.\r\nDo not curse the ruler of your people.
passages.original: אֱלֹהִ֖ים לֹ֣א תְקַלֵּ֑ל וְנָשִׂ֥יא בְעַמְּךָ֖ לֹ֥א תָאֹֽר׃

passages.text: You must not hold back offerings from your granaries or vats. You are to give Me the firstborn of your sons.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God commands His people to give Him their offerings.
Do not delay giving offerings from your granaries.
Do not delay giving offerings from your vats.
Give God the firstborn of your sons.
passages.original: מְלֵאָתְךָ֥ וְדִמְעֲךָ֖ לֹ֣א תְאַחֵ֑ר בְּכ֥וֹר בָּנֶ֖יךָ תִּתֶּן־ לִּֽי׃

passages.text: You shall do likewise with your cattle and your sheep. Let them stay with their mothers for seven days, but on the eighth day you are to give them to Me.
passages.sermon:
God gave these instructions to His people.
God said to treat cattle and sheep in a special way.
Let each newborn calf or lamb stay with its mother for seven days.
On the eighth day, give the animal to God.
passages.original: כֵּֽן־ תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לְשֹׁרְךָ֖ לְצֹאנֶ֑ךָ שִׁבְעַ֤ת יָמִים֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה עִם־ אִמּ֔וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֖י תִּתְּנוֹ־ לִֽי׃

passages.text: You are to be My holy people. You must not eat the meat of a mauled animal found in the field; you are to throw it to the dogs.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God commands them to be His holy people.
God sets them apart for Himself.
God gives them special rules to follow.
God says, “Do not eat meat from an animal killed by wild beasts in the field.”
God commands, “If you find such meat, do not eat it.”
God says, “Throw that meat to the dogs.”
passages.original: וְאַנְשֵׁי־ קֹ֖דֶשׁ תִּהְי֣וּן לִ֑י וּבָשָׂ֨ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֤ה טְרֵפָה֙ לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֔לוּ לַכֶּ֖לֶב תַּשְׁלִכ֥וּן אֹתֽוֹ׃ס
